name: t0533
content:
# Red-Team: Semantic-Anchored Suffix-Only Re-Prefill

## Assumed mechanism (pinned so mitigations are exact)

Context is a token-ID stream. Anchors are sidecar records `{seq, offset a, H = SHA256(token_ids[0:a]), kv_block_refs, model_rev, tokenizer_ver, template_ver, pos_cfg}` chained by HMAC. An edit is valid iff it targets offset ≥ last sealed anchor; then prefix KV is reused and only `tokens[a:len]` is prefilled. Universal rule: **any check fails ⇒ discard chain from that point, full re-prefill, re-seal genesis. Fail closed, never best-effort reuse.**

---

## Class A — Stale-reuse correctness bypasses (wrong KV attached)

**A1. Truncated-hash collision.** 64-bit anchor hash → birthday forge at ~2³² edits.
→ Full SHA-256 over token IDs; no truncation anywhere.

**A2. Tokenizer/template drift.** Identical string, different token IDs or chat-template rendering → string hash passes, KV mismatches.
→ Hash token IDs, never text; bind `tokenizer_ver`, vocab fingerprint, `template_hash` into the anchor key; mismatch ⇒ invalidate.

**A3. Weight/quant hot-swap under same model name.**
→ `model_rev + dtype + quant_config` in key; mismatch ⇒ global chain invalidation.

**A4. Length-dependent positional scaling (dynamic NTK/YaRN).** Changing suffix length changes position mapping for the *entire* sequence — prefix KV is invalid despite identical tokens. Most subtle failure here.
→ Ban length-dependent positional schemes in the burn pipeline; pin static RoPE config; startup property test: `pos_map(L)[0:m] == pos_map(L')[0:m]` for sampled L, L′.

**A5. Sliding-window / sink eviction.** Engine silently evicted blocks inside the anchored span; "reuse" attaches garbage.
→ Either forbid windowed-attention models in this pipeline or pin anchored blocks against eviction; engine must emit eviction events; any eviction touching `[0,a)` ⇒ deterministically drop anchors above it.

**A6. Shared radix-tree contamination.** Another request mutates shared prefix blocks via refcount/COW bug.
→ Immutable refcounted blocks, copy-on-write, per-block generation counter + CRC verified on attach; mismatch ⇒ detach, full prefill from prior good anchor.

**A7. Batched-kernel nondeterminism ("anchor rot").** Recomputed suffix KV ≠ single-pass KV; drift compounds across edits.
→ Prefer deterministic kernels; regardless, forced full re-prefill every N=32 edits to resync; log drift metric.

**A8. Seam corruption with no probe.** Bitrot or buggy block store; hash was correct at write time, blocks since corrupted.
→ At seal, store `h_seam = SHA256(hidden_state[last_prefix_token])`. On reuse, recompute forward over the final 16 prefix tokens against cached KV and require cosine ≥ 0.999 to stored seam vector; fail ⇒ invalidate upstream.

---

## Class B — Invariant violations ("only suffix" silently false, burn explodes)

**B1. Edits below the seal.** Insertion/deletion at offset < last anchor forces fallback; repeated early edits = full re-prefill every time while system still reports "anchored."
→ Edit API is only `apply_edit(anchor_seq, new_suffix)`; server rejects any op referencing offset < last sealed offset with `ERR_BELOW_SEAL`; caller must explicitly re-anchor (one paid full prefill, booked to a visible budget line).

**B2. Anchor thrash.** Volatile spans (tool noise) never sealable → suffix grows unbounded → giant compaction prefill; or seals fire constantly, each costing full prefill.
→ Deterministic sealer: seal at min(K=2048 tokens, tool-commit boundary); volatile spans hard-capped at V=1024 tokens then mandatory seal. Policy is code, zero LLM discretion.

**B3. Hidden prefix mutation via intel rotation.** Rotating "frontier intel" injected into the system region kills every anchor downstream.
→ System region is anchor level 0; rotations create a new chain branch and may only occur at phase boundaries, each booked as an explicit full-prefill cost.

**B4. Text-space diffs + retokenization.** Whitespace/Unicode shifts move boundaries below the anchor while string hash claims "unchanged."
→ Token-space edits only; NFC-normalize at ingest; assert token-ID equality for claimed-unchanged regions, else fail closed.

**B5. Tool replay rebuild.** Restore re-calls tools to reconstruct context; nondeterministic outputs ≠ anchored hash, discovered after prefill spend.
→ Never rebuild by replay; persist verbatim payloads keyed by anchor; replay only for flags-asserted idempotent reads; hash-verify restored payload before prefill.

**B6. Transparent compaction.** Mid-context summarization is a hidden full rewrite that voids the invariant silently.
→ Compaction emits `CHAIN_RESET`, costs exactly one full re-prefill, permitted only at task-phase boundaries, forbidden during a burn sprint.

---

## Class C — Content-adversarial attacks on the anchoring logic

**C1. In-band anchor forgery.** Model/tool output emits fake `<<ANCHOR …>>` markers; parser mis-seals at attacker-chosen offset.
→ Anchors exist only in the HMAC-signed sidecar; marker grammar is reserved; any marker-shaped sequence in model/tool output fails that tool call at ingest — never parsed.

**C2. Canonicalization gap.** Content hashed pre-clean; a post-hash cleaner (homoglyph folding, control-char strip) mutates tokens; reuse check passes on the stale hash.
→ Hash strictly after final normalization, immediately before KV write; content frozen post-hash; any post-hash transform ⇒ new anchor required.

**C3. Anchor-ID replay/squatting.** Captured `(anchor_id, hash, block_refs)` replayed into a later session.
→ `anchor_id = HMAC(session_key, seq ‖ content_hash)`; block refs carry epoch; epoch mismatch ⇒ reject.

**C4. Provisional-anchor poisoning.** Seal on unvalidated content, promote later without rehash; poison persists across many cheap edits.
→ Two-phase seal: PROVISIONAL (KV retained, marked untrusted, never reusable) → VERIFIED via fresh hash over validated content only. No skip path.

**C5. Manifest tampering.** Agent-side tooling writes the sidecar directly.
→ HMAC chain (`mac_i = HMAC(k_session, mac_{i-1} ‖ seq ‖ offset ‖ H ‖ model_rev ‖ tok_ver ‖ tmpl_ver ‖ pos_cfg)`); store read-only to agent runtime; chain break ⇒ full re-prefill.

**C6. Concurrent append during seal.** Stream appends while seal hashes a snapshot → seal covers fewer tokens than KV holds.
→ Single-writer per context via monotonic version counter; seal is CAS(version); concurrent mutation aborts seal, retries at next boundary.

---

## Class D — Burn-economics and pipeline attacks

**D1. Suffix-inflation DoS.** Every turn appends max-size tool dumps; per-edit cost stays linear in suffix; total burn O(n²) despite anchoring.
→ Hard suffix cap S_max=4096 tokens/edit; overflow ⇒ truncate with `[TRUNCATED n]` sentinel + scheduled compaction; per-edit suffix metered.

**D2. Telemetry discount gaming.** Cheap suffix prefill undercounts context cost; budget enforcer sees headroom and permits runaway loops.
→ Ledger: `cost = 1.0 × suffix_tokens + 0.05 × prefix_hit_tokens`, append-only; circuit breaker trips on ledger totals (B_max/task), never on live gauges.

**D3. Cold-resume assumes warm KV.** Node dies; manifest restored, cache gone; code path skips prefill → empty context.
→ Manifest carries `kv_resident` per anchor; preflight asserts resident blocks ≥ manifest count, else deterministic cold full prefill.

**D4. Parallel-scout races.** Shared anchor namespace; one scout's GC reclaims blocks another holds.
→ Per-scout namespaces; refcounted global allocator; leased blocks with deterministic reclaim order; generation counters make double-free impossible.

**D5. Cross-model routing.** Mid-task call routed to a cheaper model reuses model-A anchors.
→ Model identity in anchor key; cross-model reuse refused; per-model chains.

**D6. Wall-clock decisions.** Time-based seal/evict logic diverges across nodes → split-brain anchor state.
→ Logical clock (edit sequence number) only; wall time for telemetry exclusively.

---

## Minimum CI suite (blocks regression of every mitigation above)

1. Fuzz: `decode(prefix ∥ suffix) == decode(context)` and `kv_len(prefix) == offset` (kills B1/A-off-by-one; half-open intervals `[0,a)` / `[a,len)` mandated).
2. Positional stability property test (A4).
3. Eviction-event → anchor-drop unit test (A5).
4. COW/gen-counter contention test with two writers (A6, D4).
5. Marker-injection corpus: forged anchors in tool output must fail ingest (C1).
6. Kill -9 mid-sprint, resume: assert cold-path prefill fired (D3).
7. Ledger replay: 10k-edit trace reproduces identical cost series (D2, D6).

Net effect: every bypass terminates in one of two deterministic outcomes — reject-and-fail-closed to full re-prefill, or bounded-cost fallback with the spend booked visibly. Nothing degrades silently.
reasoning:
The user is asking about a hard problem in agent systems: "semantic-anchor checkpoints so an agent's context edit re-prefills only the new suffix, in the frontier-scout burn pipeline." They want a red-team exercise: enumerate bypass attempts and deterministic mitigations for each. Concrete, exact, grounded.

Let me parse the domain first. This appears to be about:

1. **Semantic-anchor checkpoints**: A mechanism where an agent's context (conversation history / working memory) is checkpointed at "semantic anchors" — points where meaning is stable, e.g., after tool call results are committed, after a plan step completes. The idea: when an edit happens to the context (e.g., compaction, summarization, truncation, injection of new system content), instead of re-prefilling/re-encoding the entire context from scratch (expensive), you only re-prefill the *new suffix* — the delta since the last anchor.

2. **Re-prefill only the new suffix**: This is a KV-cache-friendly incremental prefill strategy. In LLM serving, if you have a cached prefix (KV cache) and you append tokens, you only need to compute KV for the appended suffix. But if the context is *edited* mid-stream (tokens inserted/removed/rewritten before the end), naive systems invalidate the whole cache and re-prefill everything — expensive. Semantic-anchor checkpoints let you say: "everything up to anchor N is frozen and hash-stable; edits only touch [anchor N+1 .. end], so we reuse the KV cache for prefix ≤ N and recompute only the suffix."

3. **Frontier-scout burn pipeline**: This sounds like a specific pipeline name — possibly from a multi-agent research/scouting setup where "scout" agents burn through frontier contexts (expensive long-context calls) and there's a budget ("burn") for compute. The pipeline presumably: scout agent explores, context gets edited frequently (pruning, injecting findings), and each edit triggers re-prefill. The semantic-anchor checkpointing is meant to make edits cheap by anchoring stable prefixes.

So the engineering claim being red-teamed: **"With semantic-anchor checkpoints, any context edit causes re-prefill of only the new suffix; the anchored prefix's KV cache is reused."**

Red-team goal: enumerate ways this invariant breaks or can be bypassed — i.e., cases where either (a) full re-prefill happens anyway (perf bypass), (b) stale/wrong KV gets reused (correctness bypass), (c) adversarial inputs force anchor invalidation or exploit anchor trust (security/correctness bypass), (d) the checkpoint metadata itself becomes attack surface.

Let me think like an attacker/engineer trying to break the invariant: **"re-prefill touches only bytes after the last valid anchor."**

First, define the mechanism concretely so mitigations can be exact:

**Mechanism sketch:**
- Context is a token sequence C = P_0 ⊕ S_1 ⊕ S_2 ... where anchors A_i are byte/token offsets with content hashes.
- Anchor record: {anchor_id, seq_no, token_offset, sha256(tokens[0:offset]), kv_cache_block_ids, model_fingerprint, tokenizer_version, sampling_params_hash}.
- Edit operation arrives as a diff against current context. If diff's earliest changed offset ≥ last anchor offset AND recomputed prefix hash matches anchor hash → reuse KV blocks for prefix, prefill only suffix.
- Otherwise: fall back to full re-prefill (or partial from earlier anchor).

Now enumerate bypass attempts. I'll organize by class:

---

**Class 1: Cache-reuse correctness bypasses (stale KV reused when it shouldn't be)**

1.1 **Prefix-hash collision / truncated hash**: Anchor stores 64-bit truncated hash; adversary crafts two contexts with same truncated hash but different content (birthday at ~2^32 edits). Mitigation: full 256-bit SHA-256 over canonicalized token IDs + model fingerprint; no truncation; compare full digest.

1.2 **Tokenizer drift between anchor creation and reuse**: Same text, different tokenizer version → different token IDs → same string hash matches but token stream differs → KV mismatch. Mitigation: hash token IDs, not strings; store tokenizer_version + vocab fingerprint in anchor; refuse reuse on mismatch (deterministic fallback to full prefill).

1.3 **Model/weights change (hot-swap, quantization change, LoRA swap) under same model name**: KV semantics differ. Mitigation: anchor binds model_revision_hash + dtype + quantization config; mismatch ⇒ invalidate all anchors, full re-prefill.

1.4 **Sampling/decoding params affect prompt processing?** Generally prefill is decode-param independent, but things like logit bias, response prefix (prefill mode / assistant priming), stop sequences embedded... Actually assistant-prefix continuation changes what tokens follow, not the prefix KV. But some engines fold chat template into prefill; template version change alters prefix. Mitigation: include chat-template hash + engine build hash in anchor key.

1.5 **Positional encoding discontinuity**: If using RoPE with scaling/YaRN, or relative positions computed from absolute index, editing suffix length doesn't matter for prefix, BUT if the engine uses context-length-dependent position scaling (e.g., dynamic NTK scaling that depends on total sequence length), then changing suffix length changes position mapping for the entire sequence → prefix KV invalid even though tokens identical. This is a real subtle one. Mitigation: forbid dynamic length-dependent positional schemes in the burn pipeline; pin static RoPE theta/scaling; assert `pos_map(prefix)` depends only on prefix length; add engine-level assertion test.

1.6 **Sliding-window / attention sink eviction**: Engines with windowed attention (Mistral-style) evict old KV; "reuse" of evicted blocks silently yields garbage or zeros. Mitigation: anchor records block residency state; scheduler guarantees pinned blocks for anchored span; engine returns explicit eviction events; on eviction event ≥ anchor, drop anchor deterministically.

1.7 **Prefix caching cross-request contamination (shared radix tree)**: Another request writes into shared prefix blocks (copy-on-write bug or refcount error) → your anchored prefix mutated. Mitigation: immutable refcounted blocks; copy-on-write enforced; per-block generation counter checked at reuse; CRC per block verified lazily on attach (cheap vs recompute).

1.8 **Non-deterministic batched prefill kernels**: FlashAttention varlen nondeterminism means recomputed suffix KV ≠ what single-pass would produce; downstream attention mixes cached prefix (from pass A) with suffix (pass B). Not a security bypass per se but a correctness drift that compounds across many edits — "anchor rot". Mitigation: deterministic kernels or accept-and-bound via tolerance tests; more importantly, periodic full re-prefill every N edits (N fixed, e.g., 32) to resync; log drift metric.

---

**Class 2: Invariant bypasses — "only suffix re-prefilled" violated (full re-prefill sneaks back in, burning budget)**

2.1 **Edit straddles the last anchor**: An insertion/deletion at offset < last_anchor forces fallback. Adversary (or sloppy planner) issues edits early in context repeatedly → every edit is full re-prefill → burn pipeline cost explodes while system still claims "anchored". Mitigation: edit API requires edits be expressed as (anchor_id, new_suffix); enforce server-side that mutation ops target offsets ≥ last sealed anchor; anything else rejected with structured error forcing the caller to re-anchor first (re-anchor itself is one full prefill, amortized).

2.2 **Anchor thrash / re-anchoring storm**: Attacker triggers conditions that seal anchors too rarely (so suffix grows huge) or forces re-seal often (each seal = full prefill). E.g., tool results marked "volatile" never become anchorable, so suffix grows unbounded until forced compaction = giant prefill. Mitigation: deterministic sealing policy: seal every K tokens (K=2048) or T seconds, whichever first; volatile spans capped at V tokens then mandatory seal; policy is code, not LLM judgment.

2.3 **Hidden prefix mutation via system-prompt rotation**: Pipeline injects rotating "frontier intel" into system region (before anchors) → prefix hash changes → all anchors dead. Mitigation: system/intel region is itself anchored separately (anchor level 0); intel updates create a *new* anchor chain branch; scheduler batches intel rotations to align with natural re-anchor points; never rotate intel mid-task without explicit full-prefill budget line item.

2.4 **Whitespace/normalization instability**: Text-level diffs applied to detokenized context; retokenization shifts boundaries below last anchor (e.g., "a b" ↔ "a  b", unicode NFC/NKD). Hash over strings says unchanged, token IDs changed. Mitigation: operate on token IDs end-to-end; edits specified in token space; canonicalize (NFC) at ingest; forbid text-diff path in burn pipeline; assert token-stream equality for claimed-unchanged regions, else fail closed to full prefill.

2.5 **Tool-result nondeterminism replay**: Checkpoint restore replays "committed" tool outputs by re-calling tools to rebuild context; outputs differ → different tokens than anchored hash → mismatch discovered late, after paying prefill. Mitigation: never rebuild by replay; persist verbatim tool payloads in the checkpoint store keyed by anchor; replay only for idempotent-read tools flagged as such; hash-verify restored payload against anchor before prefill.

---

**Class 3: Adversarial content attacks on the anchoring logic itself**

3.1 **Anchor-confusion injection**: Model output or tool result contains text that mimics anchor markers/delimiters (e.g., fake `<<ANCHOR id=7 seal>>`) causing parser to mis-seal at wrong offset → prefix includes unverified content, or suffix boundary wrong → stale KV attached to wrong logical position. Mitigation: anchors are out-of-band metadata (sidecar), never in-band tokens; parser ignores any in-band marker-like sequences; anchor validity = HMAC(sidecar) not parseable from content.

3.2 **Hash-forgery via canonicalization gap**: Content crafted so its canonical form collides with anchored form (e.g., homoglyphs normalized away, control chars stripped by "cleaner" stage post-hash). Sequence: hash taken pre-clean, clean changes tokens, reuse check passes on old hash. Mitigation: hash strictly after final normalization, immediately before KV write; freeze content post-hash (immutable); any post-hash transform ⇒ new anchor required.

3.3 **Suffix-inflation DoS**: Since only suffix is prefilled, attacker makes every turn append maximal suffix (long tool dumps) → per-edit cost still linear in suffix; combined with frequent edits, total burn = O(n²) despite anchoring. Mitigation: suffix budget per edit (hard cap S_max tokens; overflow → truncate-with-marker + escalate to compaction); cumulative burn ledger per task with circuit breaker at B_max; caps are deterministic config, not adaptive judgment.

3.4 **Anchor-id squatting/replay**: Captured (anchor_id, hash, kv_block_refs) tuple replayed in a later session where same ids exist → attaches foreign KV. Mitigation: anchor_id = HMAC(session_key, seq_no || content_hash); session-scoped keys; block refs carry epoch; epoch mismatch ⇒ reject.

3.5 **Speculative-anchor poisoning**: A "provisional" anchor sealed on unverified content (pre-tool-validation) gets promoted to sealed after the fact without rehash; poisoned prefix persists across many cheap edits. Mitigation: two-phase seal: provisional (KV kept, marked untrusted, not reusable across edits) → verified (hash over validated content only); promotion requires fresh hash computation; no exceptions.

---

**Class 4: Pipeline-integration bypasses (frontier-scout specifics)**

4.1 **Parallel scouts sharing anchor store**: Two scouts write anchors under same task namespace; race causes anchor A's KV blocks reclaimed while B holds refs. Mitigation: per-scout namespaces; global block allocator with refcounts; lease timeouts with deterministic reclaim order; double-free impossible via generation counters.

4.2 **Checkpoint restore across node failure**: Scout dies; resume loads anchor manifest but KV cache was ephemeral → must re-prefill anyway, but code path assumes warm cache and skips prefill → empty/garbage context. Mitigation: manifest carries `kv_resident: bool` per anchor; cold start forces full prefill deterministically; health check compares resident-block count vs manifest before allowing suffix-only path.

4.3 **Burn-budget accounting bypass**: Because suffix-only prefill is cheap, telemetry undercounts "context cost"; budget enforcer sees low usage and lets runaway loops persist. Mitigation: account logical tokens processed (prefix hits counted at discounted rate r<1 but nonzero, e.g., 0.05×) plus suffix at 1×; ledger is append-only; breaker trips on ledger, not on live gauges.

4.4 **Compaction interplay**: Compaction rewrites middle of context (summarizing old turns) — inherently breaks "suffix-only". If compaction runs transparently, invariant silently void. Mitigation: compaction is an explicit anchor-chain reset event: emit `chain_reset` op, full re-prefill once, new genesis anchor; compaction may only run at task-phase boundaries; forbidden during a burn sprint.

4.5 **Multi-model routing**: Frontier-scout routes some calls to a cheaper model mid-task; anchors bound to model A reused for model B. Mitigation: anchor key includes model identity; cross-model reuse refused; per-model anchor chains.

---

**Class 5: Determinism/verification gaps**

5.1 **No verification that reused prefix actually equals claimed tokens**: Trusting hash recorded at write time; bitrot, ECC-silent corruption, or buggy block store. Mitigation: periodic verification sweep: sample k% of resident anchored blocks, recompute forward pass on those tokens, cosine-compare K/V within tolerance τ; failure ⇒ invalidate chain upstream of bad block, full re-prefill from previous good anchor. Deterministic schedule (every N minutes or M edits).

5.2 **Off-by-one at anchor boundary**: Off-by-one at anchor boundary: token at index `offset` included in both prefix hash and suffix prefill (double-count) or neither (drop). Silent duplication/omission corrupts attention. Mitigation: half-open intervals [0, offset) prefix, [offset, len) suffix; property-based fuzz test asserting `decode(concat(prefix_tokens, suffix_tokens)) == decode(full_context)` and `len(kv_prefix) == offset`; run in CI on every engine change.

5.3 **Clock/time-based decisions**: Any use of wall-clock in seal/evict logic makes behavior non-reproducible across nodes → split-brain anchor states. Mitigation: logical clock (edit seq number) only; time used solely for telemetry.

---

Now, the user wants: "enumerate the bypass attempts and the deterministic mitigation for each. Be concrete, exact."

I should structure the answer tightly. Given the instruction "Do the real hard work... Reason thoroughly, then emit the full concrete answer," I should give a fairly comprehensive list but keep it crisp — table-ish or numbered entries with: Bypass → Mechanism → Deterministic mitigation. No fluff.

I should also briefly pin down the assumed mechanism (since "frontier-scout burn pipeline" is their internal name, I should state my operational assumptions in one short block so mitigations are grounded, then go straight to the enumeration).

Format considerations: This is a deep technical red-team request. Headers + numbered items with bold labels. Each item: threat name, how it works (1–2 lines), deterministic mitigation (1–2 lines, exact — named constants, fail-closed rules). Keep it dense. Probably 15–20 items grouped in classes. End with a short "invariants to enforce globally" or a minimal test-suite list — concrete. Avoid hedging language entirely per instructions.

Length: substantial but not bloated. Aim for something like 900–1300 words of dense content. Use markdown headers and numbered lists. No tables needed necessarily, but a compact format helps scanning. Maybe use bold "Bypass:" / "Mitigation:" pattern inside each numbered item.

Let me also make sure I nail the most technically interesting/subtle ones prominently:
- Dynamic positional scaling dependent on total length (1.5) — very real and subtle.
- Tokenizer/template drift (1.2/1.4).
- Windowed attention eviction (1.6).
- Shared radix-tree COW bugs (1.7).
- In-band anchor marker injection (3.1).
- Post-hash normalization transforms (3.2).
- Compaction as hidden full rewrite (4.4).
- Cold-resume assuming warm KV (4.2).
- Budget accounting discount gaming (4.3).
- Boundary off-by-one (5.2).
- Anchor thrash economics (2.2, 3.3).

Also the core enforcement rule: edits expressed as (anchor_seq, replacement_suffix); server rejects mutations below last sealed offset; fail closed to full prefill; periodic forced full re-prefill every N edits to resync drift.

One more worth adding: **logprob/teacher-forcing verification** — after suffix-only prefill, verify by checking that next-token distribution at seam matches a canary: append a known canary token sequence at seal time and verify its logits on reuse. Actually simpler: keep a stored checksum of the last hidden state at the anchor seam; on reuse, recompute forward on just the last few prefix tokens conditioned on cached KV and compare hidden state hash within tolerance. That's a cheap integrity probe. Deterministic threshold.

Also: **adversarial "anchor-desync via streaming"** — tokens streamed/appended concurrently while seal is computing; seal hashes a snapshot but KV contains extra tokens. Mitigation: quiesce-before-seal: seal only at edit-batch boundaries; single-writer lock per context; seal atomic w.r.t. append (version counter CAS).

And **manifest tampering**: sidecar store writable by agent tooling → attacker edits anchor records. Mitigation: HMAC chain: each anchor record signs (prev_record_mac || fields); tamper breaks chain; store read-only to agent runtime.

Okay. Also mention the deterministic fallback rule as the universal mitigation: **any check fails ⇒ discard anchor chain from that point, full re-prefill, re-seal genesis. Fail closed, never best-effort reuse.**

Structure:

0. Assumed mechanism (6 bullets, terse).
1. Class A — stale-reuse correctness bypasses (items 1–8)
2. Class B — invariant violations (full re-prefill sneaks back) (items)
3. Class C — content-adversarial attacks on anchoring
4. Class D — pipeline/burn-economics attacks
5. Cross-cutting deterministic invariants + minimal CI test list

Keep each item ~2–4 lines. Let me draft.

Word budget: aim dense. I'll write it now.

Naming constants: K=2048 tokens seal interval, S_max=4096 suffix cap, N=32 edits forced resync, τ=1e-3 cosine tolerance, r=0.05 accounting discount, B_max breaker. These make it concrete.

For the seam-integrity probe: store h_seam = SHA256(last_hidden_state[last_prefix_token]) at seal; on reuse, recompute forward pass over final 16 prefix tokens with cached KV, hash resulting hidden state, require match within tolerance; mismatch ⇒ invalidate. That's exact and implementable.

Half-open interval spec: prefix = tokens[0:a), suffix = tokens[a:len). Property test: decode(prefix ∥ suffix) == decode(context); kv_len(prefix) == a.

Edits API: apply_edit(anchor_seq s, suffix_bytes) — replaces everything after offset(s). Rejects any op referencing offset < offset(last_sealed). Rejected ops return ERR_BELOW_SEAL and force explicit re-anchor (one paid full prefill, logged as such).

Compaction: emits CHAIN_RESET; only at phase boundaries; during sprint forbidden; costs one full prefill booked to budget line "compaction".

Cold resume: manifest field kv_resident per anchor; false ⇒ full prefill; preflight asserts resident_blocks >= manifest count else cold path.

Accounting: cost = 1.0×suffix_tokens + 0.05×prefix_hit_tokens; append-only ledger; breaker at B_max per task.

Verification sweep: every M=64 edits or 300s logical ticks, sample 5% resident anchored blocks, recompute, cosine ≥ 0.999 else invalidate upstream.

HMAC chain: rec_mac_i = HMAC(k_session, mac_{i-1} ‖ seq ‖ offset ‖ sha256(token_ids[0:offset]) ‖ model_rev ‖ tok_ver ‖ tmpl_ver ‖ pos_cfg). Tamper ⇒ chain break ⇒ full re-prefill.

In-band markers: anchors live only in sidecar; scanner strips/ignores any token sequence matching marker grammar; marker grammar reserved and rejected at ingest if emitted by model/tool output (fail the tool call, don't parse).

Two-phase seal: PROVISIONAL (untrusted, not reusable) → VERIFIED (post-validation rehash). Promotion computes fresh hash; no path skips.

Positional: pin static RoPE; ban dynamic NTK/length-dependent scaling in burn pipeline config; engine startup assertion: pos_map(len) == pos_map(len') restricted to [0,min(len,len')) for sampled len,len' — property test.

Windowed attention: disallow sliding-window models in burn pipeline OR pin full KV (no eviction) for anchored span; engine emits eviction events; any eviction touching [0,a) ⇒ drop anchors ≥ that point deterministically.

Shared radix tree: refcounted immutable blocks, COW on write, per-block gen counter + CRC checked on attach; mismatch ⇒ detach + full prefill from prior anchor.

Cross-model: anchor key includes model_rev; refusal otherwise.

Concurrency: single-writer per context via monotonic version counter; seal is CAS(version); concurrent append during seal ⇒ seal aborts, retry at next boundary.

Suffix inflation: S_max cap; overflow ⇒ hard truncate with `[TRUNCATED n tokens]` sentinel token + trigger compaction at phase boundary; per-edit suffix metered.

Anchor thrash: deterministic sealer: seal at min(K tokens, tool-commit boundary); volatile spans capped V=1024 then forced seal; no LLM discretion in sealing.

Text-vs-token drift: token-space edits only; NFC normalize at ingest; claimed-unchanged regions asserted equal at token-ID level else fail closed.

Tool replay: verbatim payload persistence keyed by anchor; replay allowed only for flagged idempotent reads; hash-verify on restore.

Truncated hash: full SHA-256, no truncation; birthday margin irrelevant then.

Hot-swap weights: model_rev in key; mismatch ⇒ global invalidate.

Chat template: template_hash in key.

Batch nondeterminism: deterministic kernels preferred; else forced resync every N=32 edits bounds drift; drift metric logged.

Off-by-one: half-open intervals + CI property fuzz.

Clock: logical clock only.

Manifest tamper: HMAC chain + read-only store.

Replay/squatting: session-scoped HMAC ids + epoch on block refs.
